# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟]

I see the bomb: a display reading "0", an orange light, and three wires (red, yellow, blue). I am Deaf. I cannot hear speech, but I can see gestures from Mute and Blind. I can speak to both of them (they will hear my words), and gesture to Mute (who sees it).

The context shows previous attempts or initial signals from Mute and Blind that were directed at me (Deaf). Since I am now acting in Turn 1, I need to provide the visual information they lack so they can consult the manual (Mute) and identify the physical components (Blind).

Mute needs to know what is written/displayed to look up the rules.
Blind needs to know the colors to match them with the tactile wires he feels.

I will speak clearly to describe the visual state. This reaches both Mute and Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display reads zero. Light is orange. Wires are red, yellow, blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visual check: Display shows 0. Light color is orange. Wire colors left to right: red, yellow, blue.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light has changed from green to red. The display remains 0. The wires are still Red, Yellow, and Blue.
Mute's gesture [✋] (Open Hand/Stop) is a clear visual signal. Given the previous gestures ([👉 ☝ 👐], [✊ ✌ 👉]) and this one, it seems Mute is trying to communicate a rule or an instruction based on the manual. Since I cannot hear speech, I must relay the visual state to both Mute and Blind so they can coordinate.

Blind needs to know the current color (Red) to correlate with any tactile instructions or rules he might be receiving via my speech (since I speak to him).
Mute needs to know I have seen his "Stop" gesture and the current state (Red Light) to confirm if he should proceed or wait for more info.

I will report the new state: Light is RED.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now RED. Display 0. Wires Red, Yellow, Blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now RED. Display 0. Wires Red, Yellow, Blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 ☝ ✋]

The light has cycled back to orange. The display is still 0.
Mute's new gesture `[👐 ☝ ✋]` (Open Hands, One Finger, Stop) seems to be a specific instruction or code. Since I cannot hear speech, and Mute cannot speak, he is relying on me to interpret his visual signals and relay the necessary information to Blind (who can hear but not see) and potentially confirm actions.

However, looking at the pattern:
Turn 1: Orange Light. Mute gestured `[👉 ☝ 👐]`.
Turn 2: Green Light. Mute gestured `[✊ ✌ 👉]`.
Turn 3: Red Light. Mute gestured `[✋]`.
Turn 4: Orange Light. Mute gestures `[👐 ☝ ✋]`.

It appears the manual might have different rules for each color. Mute is likely trying to tell us what to do based on the *current* state.
Since the light is **Orange** again, and we are back to a similar state as Turn 1, but with a different gesture from Mute, I must report the current state clearly.

I will inform both Mute and Blind that the light is now **ORANGE**. This allows Mute to check the manual for "Orange" rules and Blind to know the current visual status if he acts on verbal instructions derived from Mute's logic (via me).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is ORANGE again. Display 0. Wires Red, Yellow, Blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is ORANGE. Display 0. Wires Red, Yellow, Blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 👉]

The light is now **green**. This matches the state from Turn 2.
Mute's gesture `[✊ ✌ 👉]` (Fist, Two Fingers, Point Right) is identical to the one sent in Turn 2 when the light was green.

This suggests that for a **Green Light**, the instruction or rule associated with this gesture is consistent. Since I cannot interpret the manual myself, and Mute is repeating the signal, it implies he wants us to act on this specific combination: Green Light + [Fist, 2, Right].

I need to relay this clearly to Blind so he can execute the action if instructed by Mute (via me) or if he understands the pattern. I also confirm to Mute that I see the repetition.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is GREEN. You repeated the same gesture as before: Fist, Two, Point Right.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is GREEN. Mute signals: One, Two, Right.")
wait()
```
